skill.name: database-operations
skill.description: Guidance for writing efficient, maintainable SQLAlchemy database operations.
skill.summary: Promotes bulk SQLAlchemy operations, joins, and repository-based database access.
skill.author: Crossbill-Highlights

security_audit.summary: The only static finding is a false positive. SKILL.md line 6 gives normal SQLAlchemy performance guidance about bulk operations and joins, with no evidence of reconnaissance or malicious intent.

static_findings.snippet: - Avoid for-loops. Instead always prefer bulk operations using SQLAlchemy's built-in methods or use

finding_verdicts.reason: The line recommends SQLAlchemy bulk operations and SQL joins to avoid inefficient loops. It does not request system inspection, environment discovery, or data collection.

content.value_statement: Database code can become slow when queries run inside repeated loops. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code toward bulk SQLAlchemy operations, joins, and repository boundaries.
actual_capabilities: Guides SQLAlchemy database operations toward efficient query patterns.
Recommends bulk operations instead of repeated loop-based database calls.
Encourages SQL joins to fetch related data in a single query.
Directs database access into repository classes.
Supports maintainable Python data access discussions.
limitations: Does not include detailed SQLAlchemy code examples.
Does not configure database engines, sessions, or migrations.
Does not validate schema design or indexing choices.
Does not replace application-specific performance testing.

use_cases.title: Refactor Slow Query Workflows
use_cases.description: Use the skill to identify loop-heavy database operations and convert them into bulk or joined SQLAlchemy patterns.

use_cases.title: Standardize Repository Design
use_cases.description: Use the skill to keep database operations inside repository classes across a Python service.

use_cases.title: Review Database Pull Requests
use_cases.description: Use the skill to check whether proposed database changes follow efficient and maintainable SQLAlchemy practices.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Query Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this SQLAlchemy database workflow and explain where loop-based database calls should be replaced with bulk operations.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor Repository Logic
prompt_templates.prompt: Suggest a repository-based design for this database operation while keeping SQLAlchemy queries efficient and maintainable.

prompt_templates.title: Reduce Related-Data Queries
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this data loading workflow and recommend joins or set-based operations that avoid repeated related-record queries.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Data Access Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this database workflow for inefficient loops, missing repository boundaries, and opportunities for bulk SQLAlchemy operations.

output_examples.input: A feature updates many account records one at a time inside a loop.
output_examples.output: Recommendation: replace repeated updates with a bulk SQLAlchemy operation when business rules allow the same update shape.

output_examples.input: A service fetches orders, then queries customer details separately for each order.
output_examples.output: Recommendation: load the related data through a join or another set-based SQLAlchemy approach to reduce query count.

output_examples.input: Several services perform database writes directly instead of using a shared data access layer.
output_examples.output: Recommendation: move database operations into repository classes so query behavior stays consistent and easier to review.

best_practices: Prefer set-based SQLAlchemy operations when many records share the same database action.
Use joins for related data when they reduce repeated database round trips.
Keep database access inside repository classes for clearer ownership.
anti_patterns: Running a database query for each item in a large loop.
Placing database operations directly throughout service and controller code.
Fetching related records one at a time when a join can load them together.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps AI assistants apply efficient SQLAlchemy database operation guidelines.

faq.question: Does it generate complete database code?
faq.answer: It provides guidance, but the source skill does not include full code templates.

faq.question: Can it help reduce slow query loops?
faq.answer: Yes. It specifically recommends bulk operations instead of loop-based database calls.

faq.question: Does it support repository patterns?
faq.answer: Yes. It directs database operations to be contained in repository classes.

faq.question: Is this skill only for SQLAlchemy?
faq.answer: Yes. The documented guidance is specific to SQLAlchemy database operations.

faq.question: Can it replace performance profiling?
faq.answer: No. It gives design guidance, but real systems still need measurement and testing.
